utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see witness is not here and I was advised that Mr. Karadzic wants to raise something with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning, everybody. I wish to say for the record but also for all future trials, I wish to make clear the position of the Defence in respect of this witness and all other witnesses. I don't know if this is a precedent, but it is certainly a dangerous practice that the Prosecution has introduced; namely, to call ambitious witnesses who are their former employees and they directed their work by giving them guide-lines and now they are being presented as independent experts who come here to testify. It is my conviction that this is an instance of giving evidence by the Prosecution and not by independent experts. The written material that we are facing are the complete repetition of one aspect of the indictment and not only that; it is even more ambitious than the indictment. It is very general. There's a general distortion of facts, wrong interpretation, and it even aspires to the status of evidence. What I'm concerned with is the following: Am I to test and probe into each false fact and misinterpretation? There are hundreds of paragraphs and thousands of footnotes and all are wrong, except for those where the law is quoted. And am I expected to prove that this survey is -- isn't worth a thing? There have been five or six such witnesses already who were employees of the OTP and the OTP directed their expert work. If the Trial Chamber is to give any weight to that, then I will request for all such witnesses to be re-called for additional examination. I must say this for this trial and all future trials because I can see that there are many small countries and presidents of these countries who are expected to stand trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that it? So you completed your submission, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot go into the details now, but as we have seen and as we are about to see, namely, to what extent all this is wrong, is it necessary for me to disprove each and every paragraph to the Trial Chamber; or is it sufficient to show that on some examples? And I'm curious to know to what weight the Trial Chamber will give to this kind of evidence and if so, then I will request for them to be re-called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you here. This is an example how we are wasting the precious court time. Those witnesses who are called pursuant to Rule 94 bis, and according to the regime -- there's a regime through which you can challenge the qualification or other things. I stand corrected -- I should stand corrected if I'm wrong, but I -- as long as I can remember, you didn't challenge the qualification when there is notice from the Prosecution. And as for this witness and also with other witnesses, their scope of expert reports and their methodologies were made clear through their report. And as professional Judges, we are aware of all the points were raised which all go to the matter of weight. So there's no point to make that submission anew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: May I add one thing. You said I'm curious to know what weight the Trial Chamber will give this kind of evidence. But at this point in time we can't address that issue, can we, the Trial Chamber, the question of weight?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I believe that. But I wonder how I can defend myself if the segment of the indictment this witness has dealt with and presents it as evidence, if I only have 10 or 15 hours to test all that. It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want the Prosecution to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually Ms. Elliott who would address you on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just in terms of the issue of time, the Prosecution would point out that Mr. Karadzic has used a significant amount of time cross-examining Mr. Theunens on political matters and, in fact, he did not choose to cross-examine Mr. Treanor on these matters, who dealt directly with issues raised in cross-examination yesterday by Mr. Karadzic, as required to do so under Rule 90(H). So there is an issue of how Mr. Karadzic is organising his cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When we decide the amount of time which is necessary for your cross-examination, the Chamber carefully considers all the circumstances. And after such careful consideration we decided 11 hours for this witness for your cross-examination is appropriate. Having observed your cross-examination so far, as noted by Ms. Elliott, the Chamber is not minded to extend the time allotted to you at the moment. So let's not waste time any more. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we do that, may I just introduce my last intern for the summer, Ms. Sanja Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note that Mr. Karadzic has spent about six hours and 20 minutes so far and he will have four hours and 40 minutes. And how long would you need for your re-examination, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would think about -- at the time -- at this point in time about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I wonder whether - I'm asking the parties and staff - if it is possible to sit about -- for about an hour tomorrow, I -- around 11.00. So if -- I would appreciate if parties and staff members let us know through court deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the planning purposes, would you be available tomorrow in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I understand it would always be better than to have me fly back in August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your report presents the position that the six strategic goals are a public or secret task for the VRS and that the VRS existed and acted in order to realise these goals, to achieve them; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have already discussed this question yesterday. I have not put in my report, not concluded in my report, that the sole purpose or that the purpose of the VRS's existence was to implement the six strategic goals. What I have put in my report and what I have concluded is that the operations conducted by the VRS between its establishment, date of its establishment, and the Dayton Agreement are coherent or consistent with the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you identify any of these strategic goals as being illegitimate; and if so, which?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was not within the direction I had received to determine whether or not these goals or any of these goals were legitimate or illegitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To corroborate the position of the Defence that these were not military but political goals and that they constituted a platform for talks, let me ask you whether you agree that we were unable to establish that these strategic goals were an item on the agenda, that there was no vote on them, and that they are not to be found among the conclusions of that Assembly session? We did that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand that this is the view of Mr. Karadzic. Now, in my report in addition to the references in the minutes of the 16th Assembly Session, I have also included in footnote 163, part 2 of the report, a document signed by Mr. Krajisnik, who was the president of the Assembly, which is sent in the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and contains the six strategic goals. It's a document dated the 12th of May, 1992, reference number -- I mean on the document 02-130/92, which indicates to me that the six strategic goals were indeed disseminated or the information concerned of the six strategic goals was disseminated in the SRBiH, and yesterday I also indicated the link I see or I have analysed between the six strategic goals and the subsequent directives by the Supreme Command and/or the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But that was published in the Official Gazette in 1993; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honours. What was published in the Official Gazette in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These six strategic goals in the form of a decision, although we have seen that it was not a decision but merely information as part of my presentation. They were only published one year later; correct? They may have been dated the 12th of May, but they were published in the Official Gazette one and a half years later.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be possible, but a publication in 1993, according to my findings, does not exclude that they were also known on the 12th -- I mean, announced and known on the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was about the publication.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- it's possible, Your Honours, that they were also published in the Official Gazette in 1993, but my understanding is that the document by Krajisnik is dated 12th of May and the directives are -- I mean the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you don't know whether it was published in Official Gazette in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you can simply answer like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D428, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes from the 4th Session of the War Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the widened Presidency, held on 10 June 1992. D428. I would like to direct your attention all these items, political work among soldiers, unity of command, terminate activities in town, move a unit from Krajina because if we don't use artillery there is no strategic balance, the prohibition of mass funerals of fallen soldiers, and so on and so forth. And then item 10, that the strategic goals and the map of the Serbian BH be published and sent to the European Community. Why send it to the European Community unless it's meant to be a platform for negotiations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first time I see this document. I cannot establish why Mr. Karadzic instructed that the strategic goals and the maps of what is described or identified as Serbian BiH should be published and sent to the European Community. It may well be that it was intended to assist with the negotiations. But in the meanwhile we have already a first directive for further operations dated the 6th of June which identifies or sets a number of goals or tasks for the VRS which are consistent with at least five of the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While you can see the transcript part, could you assist the court reporter as to what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, my answer was in the meanwhile we have already a first directive for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Second line of your answer: "I can ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot establish or I cannot say why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- Mr. Karadzic instructed that the strategic goals ... and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't the Presidency decide about this at the session of the Presidency attended also by some persons who were not members of the Presidency, such as Mladic, Gvero, Tolimir, isn't this a decision of the Presidency to send the map and the strategic goals to the European Community? These were our negotiating positions of which we wanted to inform the European Community, our position for the continuation of talks.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, it is indeed a report of the -- or the minutes of the meeting of the expanded -- of the Presidency with a number of individuals present who are not members of the Presidency. And the conclusions reflect the view of the members of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Theunens, I must intervene with regard to semantics. This confusion between expanded Presidency or the expanded meeting -- this distinction cost Krajisnik much hard work and possibly a couple of years in prison. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your Honours, these remarks are really not needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Totally unnecessary and improper. It's time for you to put questions, not to make a statement or comment. Please bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, with all due respect, I testified in the Krajisnik case because of such semantic problems. This says expanded meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is expanded here, the Presidency or the meeting? Is it expanded by adding some people who are not members of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mentioned there are a number of people attending who are not members of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you said in your reply that it was a meeting of the expanded Presidency, whereas I say that it was instead an expanded meeting of the Presidency. One thing is an expanded Presidency. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think Mr. Theunens has answered the question. "There are a number of people attending who are not members of the Presidency." I think that tells all. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I must ask you to assist us about some of your interpretations. Did your work include qualifying my conduct or my documents? Was it your job to analyse them and present them or to state an opinion about them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to refer to the scope of the report, and I don't know whether I have to repeat it but I have mentioned it a few times over the previous days, that my task was to analyse the role of Mr. Karadzic as the highest political authority over the Bosnian Serb TO, or the SRBiH TO followed by the VRS, focussing on two aspects. The first aspect is command and control and the second aspect is situational awareness. And I then drew conclusions in relation to these two aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at page 278 where humanitarian aid is mentioned. You say that I had a monopoly in deciding about humanitarian aid because I wanted to benefit from that position in which I was to decide about the transit of convoys. It says in sub-item QQ: "The leadership of the Bosnian Serbs headed by Radovan Karadzic uses humanitarian aid to exert pressure on the other war parties and on the international community. Radovan Karadzic reminds" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's find the passage first. Can you confirm that it was --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is most helpful to always mention a footnote from this page, then it's easy to find, because we seem to have different versions. So it would be much better to address the footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Correct. Could -- Mr. Theunens has found the passage. Mr. Karadzic, what footnote are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately the OTP merged documents and then the footnote numbers were changed, so there is no correspondence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's not correct. That's what -- we did not change the footnotes. That's why the footnotes are the most helpful to identify the passage in each version that is in front of any of us. The footnotes were not changed at all, just the page numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, it's about --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It changed in the translation, the translators merged all the reports into one and the footnote -- and the footnote numbers changed automatically. That's how the Serbian version was made. The translations were merged and then the numbers of the footnotes were automatically adapted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the table of contents and can you identify where it is about -- or, Mr. Theunens, it's about monopoly of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, it -- I believe I have the same version as Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Karadzic was citing or quoting from paragraph QQ in the executive summary -- in the summary of section number 4 and this refers to information included starting at the sections footnote 1003 and following until 1028. And actually, this conclusion Mr. Karadzic read out from paragraph QQ from the summary can also be found after footnote 1028, part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we have paragraph QQ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is in the summary section of section 4 of the report, Your Honours. And, for example, the word -- I mean, I didn't use the word "monopoly," but I quoted the word "exclusively," which I found, for example, in a document signed -- or a reminder/instruction issued by Mr. Karadzic on the 17th of August, 1994 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you tell us, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, page number, para QQ? Section 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be the 14th or the 15th page of the summary section of section 4.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: In English 123, page 123, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 123 is the page in the original version and there is a merged version now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Footnote number nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This -- this is summary, Your Honours. There is no footnote there, but the first footnote that follows is 355.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps in the -- in the merged version it's the ERN number 07046594, there you find QQ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you. Yes, page 123, correct. My apologies. Yes, put your question again, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You established that I'm interfering or dealing with humanitarian issues, especially the passage of convoys, for the reasons that you mention here; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I did so on the basis of the documents I have reviewed between footnote 1004 and footnote 1028.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So your job was to review documents and to extract a qualification of my behaviour; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's an issue of translation, but as I mentioned already in the scope of the report I wanted to find out what the role was of Mr. Karadzic in relation to two aspects: Command and control, whereby I looked, for example, at whether he was issuing orders; were these orders implemented; what did he do to verify the implementation of these orders; what action did he take or not take when these orders were implemented or when the end result was different from the one he intended. Now, the second aspect, situational awareness, covered, among other things, whether Mr. Karadzic was informed of the operations or the activities of the VRS or the situation. That is not just that he receives information, but also that he gathered information himself --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But I kindly ask you now just to focus on the humanitarian issues involved, so QQ; right? Was it your job to qualify, on the basis of those documents, my behaviour in view of that particular segment? Is that what you were asked to do?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I was not asked to do that. It is me, myself, who determined that -- who established that actually control over the flow of humanitarian convoys -- I mean, that there was a control exercised in the RS -- or at first SRBiH and then the RS. And during my research I tried to find out who was responsible for the orders that imposed that control. And obviously, I came across military documents, I came across, call it, political documents, including documents signed by Mr. Karadzic or documents referring to orders by Mr. Karadzic. And on the basis of all that documentation, I drew certain conclusions and those conclusions, the summary thereof, can be found in paragraph QQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you came across texts in which I intervene to have convoys stopped or to have convoys let through?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, whereby from the documents I have reviewed it is not so much about individual convoys; it's more the policy behind these individual authorisations or prohibitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And your conclusion is that I issued orders that made it possible to create further obstacles and impede the delivery of humanitarian aid; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that I had a front line of almost 2.000 kilometres, that I had 225.000 soldiers, that I had a million and a half hungry people under sanctions, that I had 61 municipalities where the leaderships were unskillful in carrying out their work, that I had a multitude of international negotiators, that I worked until 2.00 or 3.00 at night; and now you say that I issued orders that made it possible to impede humanitarian aid. And this is what the Defence says to that: I interfered in that only at the request of the international community. Did you know that? I was asked to help and to appoint the highest possible authorities that would allow convoys to pass through.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- there's just one example, footnote 989 in Part 2 of the report, 10th of April, 1994, the Supreme Command decides to suspend all contacts between the Main Staff of the VRS and the UNPROFOR command and the Supreme Command also imposes a ban on the movement of UNPROFOR personnel and convoys, including humanitarian convoys. And this decision of the Supreme Command is included in a report by the Chief of Staff of the VRS, as I mentioned footnote 989. I mean, and there are several documents that show that Mr. Karadzic himself intervenes in granting or prohibiting freedom of movement for UNPROFOR, including humanitarian convoys as well as allowing, for example, the ICRC to meet blue helmets who had been taken hostage by the VRS in May or June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm dealing with right now: Do you accept that on the roads of Bosnia-Herzegovina every day there were about 700 trucks and in Republika Srpska it was 500 because it had the largest territory? Do you accept this information from an agency that dealt with that particular matter, that every day on the roads of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were 700 trucks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't verify that, but I have no reason to doubt the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you accept a piece of information from this institution that dealt with it as well, that during the course of 1200 days on Sarajevo airport in Serb-held territory, 20.000 aircraft landed and you can fire from there even with a pistol?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't see the link between the firing of a pistol and the 20.000 aircraft that landed or allegedly landed on Sarajevo airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that through Serb-held territory and on Serb-held territory - because the airport was within our zone - over 20.000 aircraft landed during the course of 1200 days?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. Yes, I haven't -- I mean, I haven't come across that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the percentage of convoys that had difficulties is a single-digit number? It is not 10 per cent in any conceivable way. There are very few convoys that had problems with corporals or lower-ranking officers or privates sometimes when the goods that were being transported did not have a proper declaration and so on and so forth. Do you know that on a daily basis the percentage of such trucks would have been single digit?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Karadzic is putting here a lot of information to the witness where we -- that are not in evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's not citing any reference --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, there is no reference where these claims come from. I know that he has a right to put his case to the witness, but he should not formulate it as if these were facts in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, he didn't say that it was an established fact. The witness can say no or he doesn't know if he doesn't know. Yes, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want me to answer the last question by Mr. Karadzic, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I come back to the scope of the report, I -- it was not my role to analyse the flow of humanitarian aid in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I analysed whether or not Mr. Karadzic had any authority in that matter, and then on the basis of the material I reviewed, I mentioned what material I drew conclusions as to what authority Mr. Karadzic had in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But with all due respect, Mr. Theunens, that is not correct. You established whether I had the power to do so as supreme commander, but you also presented your own point of view as to what I did with these powers. You said that I abused them. Do you know what the volume of impediments was in this enormous volume of traffic? You do not. All right. Now, do you know --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should at least give me an opportunity to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mentioned, for the purpose of this report I didn't analyse the flow of information -- the flow of humanitarian aid, I apologise, in Bosnia-Herzegovina; but I can provide examples, if needed, if the Trial Chamber wants me to do so, of what I know from prior to joining the OTP, in particular during the time I served in UNPROFOR, UNPF headquarters in Zagreb 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, now I'm talking about the QQ conclusion that you made that is accusatory and damning as far as my role in humanitarian aid is concerned, and that is why it is important for me to establish whether you established --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Karadzic, you ask the question and then if the witness doesn't agree, then that's it. Move on to another topic. You have another -- you have opportunity to argue -- to make a submission as to the credibility or the weight of that evidence later on. Don't argue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the international community, its highest representatives, including Mrs. Ogata, asked me to help in situations when some convoys were coming across obstacles at separation lines, or rather, at the front lines that they were crossing? Have you come across my correspondence with Mrs. Ogata and other representatives of UN agencies?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, not during the preparation of this report, but from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The French interpretation of the question has now -- just now completed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please start your -- could you answer now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not specifically during the preparation of this report, but I am familiar with such correspondence as well as statements by various international officials when international humanitarian convoys were subject of restrictions or freedom of movement in the territory held by the Bosnian Serbs or check-point they controlled to access, for example, the safe areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that international factors asked me to appoint a high official of Republika Srpska whose authority would not be in dispute for some sergeant at a check-point, so as to have his orders carried out, that is? Also, for that purpose I even established a committee and appointed Professor Koljevic who was the number two man in Republika Srpska to head that committee. You deal with that on page 278, co-ordination body of the Government of Republika Srpska, and you have several paragraphs there. Page 278.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it -- the committee itself is discussed in footnote 1016 and the section starts with footnote 1011.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The footnotes are changed in my version, but on the next page you say that the committee was chaired by Nikola Koljevic, vice-president of Republika Srpska, and the decision indicates that the co-ordinating body of the government was part of that committee. So at the level of the government we have a co-ordination body and at the level of the state we have a committee that is run by the number two man in the republic and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Because you are asking so many questions, we end up in many times not having a proper answer. Mr. Theunens, did you answer the question whether international -- whether you knew that international factors asked Mr. Karadzic to appoint a high official of Republika Srpska whose authority could not be in dispute for some sergeant at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that specific point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you know about the constant objections that were raised by our army because we were too permissive, too lenient, in view of the requests made for convoys to pass, convoys that included goods that were not humanitarian aid, and so on and so forth? Have you come across documents in which I quarrel with my army in terms of this leniency, although it jeopardises the security and safety of our army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, not specifically for humanitarian aid, but I have seen another document where -- it had to deal with the -- it was dealing with the implementation, I think, of the cease-fire or cessation of hostilities agreement, where some members of the VRS Main Staff opposed the appointment of international observers, I believe, but that was early in the conflict, but that's reported in -- that's included in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In sub-item 7 in this section about the co-ordination body you say that: "Throughout the 1993-1995 period, the Main Staff on an almost daily basis notified its subordinate units of its agreement with the approval given by the government for the passage of humanitarian aid convoys and of personnel through VRS-held territory, including distribution subject to inspection, or rather, restrictions, for example, limitation on amount of ..." et cetera and so on and so forth. Do you know that these were thousands of convoys and thousands of approvals and there were very few impediments that were put on their path, either by civilians or soldiers on the ground?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I included a few documents referring to impediments in footnotes 1023 to 1027. Now, for my activities outside the OTP, I mean prior to joining the OTP, mainly in the UNPROFOR/UNPF headquarters, it was out understanding there were many more impediments. And I think it is important to highlight the detailed nature of the impediments, for example, that limitations are imposed on the amount of school supplies that can be provided to the other side, if I can put it that way, or even prohibition on fuel or heating equipment to eastern enclaves, that medical equipment is confiscated, that shows a -- I would say very detailed and a very, yeah, specific intervention or even interference with the free flow of humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a flourishing trade there in these goods that we kept under our control and that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the enclaves got its supplies through this humanitarian aid. For example, fuel. Their smugglers in the enclaves smuggled those -- that fuel that we let through, they traded in that. Just yes or no. Did you know that or did you not know that? And did you take into account the fact that the restrictions placed by the army had to do with the safety and security of our army, not the needs of civilians?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the restrictions I just read out, like, for example, school supplies, school supplies don't have a military -- don't serve a military purpose --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, please, I'm asking you about fuel. I'm asking you about fuel. And I'm asking you about food. Were -- did we have an obligation to feed the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or did we have the right not to let through this food that was being sent to the army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I understand that -- what I remember from my work outside -- prior to joining the OTP, that is -- was that humanitarian aid was intended to alleviate the needs of the civilian population. There may have been misuse, but that happens in all conflicts, sadly. Now, whether -- whether -- this is -- can be a justification to stop all the flow of humanitarian aid or not, it's a matter I can't address here, it's outside my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D3908, could we please have a look at that. Have you seen evidence of our army constantly raising these objections with me, asking me why we were letting all of this get through in order to meet the needs of our enemies? This is military correspondence, military documentation, that you had to come across. Have you come across such correspondence between myself and the Main Staff, certain generals? If you're waiting for the document before you respond, that's all right --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see here General Milovanovic is saying --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document, but I was -- I mean, I only see the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English page, the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us collapse the B/C/S version for the moment. Mr. Theunens, you read the first page, let us know. It's a three-page document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read the first page, Your Honours. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's okay for the English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see 1D309, my reply to the general. 1D3909, 3909.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When everybody has read it, we can move on to the following page, but I leave that to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, next page. Can Mr. Karadzic now ask a question to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this lesson, Mr. Theunens, is this an attempt of mine to disrupt humanitarian aid or am I forced to argue with my army and tell them not to impede convoys? Have you seen this document? And if you have seen it, do you still stand by your conclusion as in item QQ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had not seen Mr. Karadzic's reply. I'm not sure whether I saw Mr. Milovanovic's document, but again from certain comments the military include in their orders to subordinates to allow the passage of humanitarian convoys, I could indeed feel or see that there was criticism towards the decisions of the committee. Now, on the other hand, I have also seen that - and I mentioned those documents - that on the orders of Mr. Karadzic the flow of humanitarian aid is stopped and that occurs, for example, at occasions when there is pressure of the international community on the Bosnian Serbs, which led me to conclude that they can use humanitarian aid as part of their strategy to achieve their goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D3908 will be Exhibit D1589 and 1D3909 will be Exhibit D1590.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you agree that on several occasions the international community opened fire on our military units and that those were the cases, two or three of them, when I stopped UN and humanitarian aid convoys, that it was always linked to the opening of fire on our army? Do you -- are you familiar with the circumstances under which I prohibited the passage of convoys?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, there are, for sure, a number of cases where indeed Mr. Karadzic or the Main Staff decides to suspend the free flow of humanitarian aid following, for example, the use of close air support or air-strikes by UNPROFOR, air-strikes provided by NATO. But again, there are also restrictions - and we read out some of them - restrictions imposed without such -- or in different situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm asking you about what you established that I stopped the convoys on some occasions. Was that just like that or was it triggered by conflicts between the VRS and international units, yes or no? Did I do it lightly or was it triggered by armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my answer was that there are indeed examples where Mr. Karadzic imposes such prohibitions after UNPROFOR has used close air support or called for air-strikes. However, there are also other examples where there were restrictions on, systematic restrictions, on the flow of humanitarian aid. And that answer is based not only on the documents included in my report but also my knowledge or my experience during the time I worked in the UNPROFOR/UNPF headquarters in Zagreb 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did you mean by different situations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example -- and again, Your Honours, this is not in my report, but we noticed there were patterns in relation to the access or free access to the airplanes to the airport of Sarajevo, patterns in the sense that fire would be opened on aircraft landing on the airport close to or during or after negotiation sessions led by international community, for example -- I mean, peace talks in Geneva or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fire by who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That could not always be established, Your Honours, but on the basis of the reports we received in the headquarters it included also fire originating from areas that were under Bosnian Serb control. And there was no possibility for a criminal or a forensic investigation of those incidents, but in that sense I have included in my report at least one order by Mr. Karadzic prohibiting the opening of fire on aircraft landing in Sarajevo airport, which suggested, at least based on the knowledge of Mr. Karadzic, some of that fire originated from the VRS. I also remember - and again I have not included in my report because I couldn't come across the documents when conducting the research here - that actually throughout the conflict -- and especially the eastern enclaves, for example, Srebrenica, the Bosnian Serb forces controlled the access to the enclave. That doesn't rule out that there were cases of black marketing between VRS and ABiH, but, for example, for the Dutch blue helmets who were deployed in Srebrenica that, almost from the beginning from their arrival, there were restrictions on food-supplies to them as well as -- that is not humanitarian aid, but still on the military equipment that they were allowed to take into the enclave. And, for example, they brought APCs to the enclave, but the VRS prohibited them from taking in the anti-tank missiles that were part of the equipment of those APCs. And this is outside my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with all due respect, I'm standing trial here and I'm asking you if, in case of armed conflict between my army and the army of the United Nations, the danger for the UN increases when they turn up at our check-points. Did you find -- did you come across any prohibition of mine that was not in the content -- within the context of armed incidents? I'm talking about my orders and not what some corporal on the ground did.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the concept of "army of the United Nations." UNPROFOR was sent as a peacekeeping force with essentially humanitarian mandate, i.e., to assist with the free flow of humanitarian --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. The concept was that there were UN forces there and that were armed incidents between the VRS and those forces. Did I ever put up obstacles outside the context of these incidents? Or was it in a situation where new incident would only have made things worse? Please answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- the witness has just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm dealing with it, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. But you formulate your question as referring to armed conflict between your army and the army of the United Nations, so Mr. Theunens was perfectly entitled to clarify the meaning. But I think he made it clear, that point. And can you kindly proceed to answer the remainder of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I reviewed do not allow to conclude whether the restrictions imposed by Mr. Karadzic were only related to the use of force, again in the framework of United Nations Security Council Resolutions, by UNPROFOR against the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You didn't establish that, but you put forward the allegation that I am responsible for that. I'm concerned by your interpretations, Mr. Theunens, but let's leave this topic now and go to other instances of this topic. It's around footnote 1165 where you deal with the Yellow Wasps. Do you know -- are you familiar with the notion of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's a paramilitary formation in Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, yes, it's -- it's Serbian volunteer group officially called a paramilitary formation who participated in the take-over in -- of Zvornik as well as the aftermath.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is no footnote 1165.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, it's been merged, but let's look at 65 ter 09220. It's a document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the document you are citing. It's a police report to the MUP headquarters at Pale about the Yellow Wasps. Could we please see it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is mentioned among others in footnote 481, part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are saying that I or the Serbian leadership is responsible for this formation that calls itself the Yellow Wasps and which you -- as you rightly say, began as a volunteer unit and later became a paramilitary unit. Did you establish that, that they initially were a volunteer unit and later became a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's all about how we defined the concepts. In Serbia they were called volunteer units, and we have established why that was done so. Now, we see that in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina orders are given to subordinate volunteer groups to the VRS or otherwise they should be removed. And then we see that for those groups who refuse to be subordinated the term "paramilitary groups" is used to identify them, which refers or emphasises their illegal character as it is used -- I mean, "paramilitary" is used for non-legal groups who are organised in a military manner and use military means or tactics to achieve certain goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the following: You're saying in one of these paragraphs that it can be seen from this what -- that the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik had the leading role in the setting up of the military structures of the Bosnian Serbs. And then you say that Vojin Vuckovic, according to the allegations in his statement, that's my footnote number 1168, but that is probably due to the merging, and Vojin Vuckovic took part in some operations and then he made a statement and so on. Are you trying to say that this paramilitary group, the Yellow Wasps, is mine and that the police arresting them is not mine?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not stated in the report that the Yellow Wasps are -- or belong to Mr. Karadzic. That's how I understand the word "mine." However, they do participate in the take-over of Zvornik at a time when there is a Bosnian Serb or SDS-led Crisis Staff in Zvornik that is issuing orders to establish military formations in Zvornik. MUP conduct a mobilisation and issues instructions for related activities. So my conclusion was that the Yellow Wasps participated in the take-over with the knowledge and approval of the Crisis Staff. And actually, footnote 476, for example, states that -- I mean, there are several groups, there is also the Zuco group, there is the Pivarski group, the Niski group, they are all identified by the Bosnian Serb authorities in Zvornik as TO of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Approval of the Crisis Staff of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly. Yes, Your Honours, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the TO of a municipality under the jurisdiction of that municipality and are volunteers a legal component of the armed forces until they break loose and become renegades?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the additional instructions and orders that were issued in June/July 1992 by the civilian and military authorities in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would agree with that proposition. Now -- sorry, if they become renegades, then you would expect the police and/or the military to ensure that law and order is being abided by and appropriate measures are taken against renegades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were such measures taken against the Yellow Wasps? Do you know that they were arrested in a well-planned operation in which nobody was killed, all 180 of them or how many there were, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I'm familiar with the fact that they were arrested. I don't recall exactly when and I don't know the number of people in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's remove this document --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if I -- if you allow me, Mr. Karadzic. I also have a recollection that there has been a trial in Serbia or an attempt of a trial in Serbia in 1994, but that that trial was not finalised then. And that most recently, I think after 2000, a new trial took place. So again, that would suggest that they were indeed arrested but released. Attempts at trial were undertaken, but then apparently they were released again. It's only most recently, after 2000, I think I was working at the OTP when a trial took place in Belgrade -- of members of the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wasn't the brother of that Vuckovic during the war sentenced to imprisonment and didn't he die in prison and didn't we ban all these people from entering the RS and didn't I order the arrest of the Yellow Wasps? Do you know any of that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't know the precise answer. I mean, the -- I see now in my report I included that actually, the trial in Serbia is covered in footnote 499, that concerns an indictment -- or it's basically an indictment that is issued against Dusko Vuckovic and also against Vojin Vuckovic, so I'm not sure which brother Mr. Karadzic is now talking about. Because according to this indictment issued by the Sabac, Serbia -- I mean, Serbia district attorney, they were still alive in April 1994. And Dusko Vuckovic was also still alive in 2005, so maybe Mr. Karadzic is talking about Vojin Vuckovic, then after 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you speak about Serb forces, do you include the Yellow Wasps and such groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I use the term "Serb forces" in the context of the take-over operations, indeed, for Zvornik I include the Yellow Wasps. And I just gave a reference of a document whereby -- indicating that the Bosnian Serb authorities in Zvornik called these volunteers members of the TO of the Serbian municipality. That was footnote 476.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this police officer, the one who's reporting, part of the Serb forces? Is he part of the government or are the Yellow Wasps a government structure?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They may be both. I mean, it depends of the moment in time and the context. The -- I understand that the police officer you referred to, footnote 481, now that's a report compiled by the Pale crime directorate of the Ministry of the Interior of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I cannot establish whether or not he or people from that department -- directorate took part in the take-over operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when you use the term "Serb forces" in the context of the take-over operation for Zvornik, is that the only instance when you use it referring to the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would have to look at what moment in time -- I mean, we would have to look at the moment in time because if the Yellow Wasps are declared a renegade group, then they're not part of anymore what I called the Serb forces. But during the take-over they are for sure part of the Serb forces. Afterwards we would have to look at the context. Because some of these groups broke away, and not just in Zvornik but also in other areas, groups that are initially part of the Serb forces conducting the take-over operation, then, yeah, go their own way or start pursuing their own goals, sometimes with support of local authorities, and then obviously their status changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the particular case of Zvornik, they arrested these authorities and that the authorities were relieved when they were arrested. When they ceased to be volunteers and became a paramilitary group, the authorities turned against them and they turned against the authorities. Did you know that when a volunteer group breaks away from the chain of command and control of the army or the police, the whole government structure from the municipal authorities up to the highest echelons of government turns against that group and eliminates it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm familiar with the orders that were issued - and I mentioned that already - by -- orders and instructions by Mr. Karadzic as well as by the command of the Main Staff. Now, we would have to look at the specific cases to see how these orders were implemented. But indeed, orders were issued to subordinate these groups or to have them removed. And I have given a few examples where groups were indeed removed. There are other examples where groups, for example, leave, come back, on the request of local authorities; and there's also the example of Arkan, for example, where Arkan comes back in -- in -- to the wider Sanski Most area in September 1995, as we saw during the examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note the time. Do we have another five minutes or ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Court deputy could approach the bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was advised that the court deputy hasn't heard from the parties whether it is possible to sit tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution is available. I, myself, will not be here, but Ms. Elliott is also prepared to do the re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we haven't actually had a chance to speak about this, but I think it would be okay. I also myself won't be here, but I believe -- certainly Dr. Karadzic will be here and I believe at least one of our case managers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break now. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, the Chamber is minded to sit for a session tomorrow from -- starting from 11.00. In that case, only two Judges will be sitting, myself and Judge Baird. I think -- we considered the matter and the Chamber is of the opinion that it's possible, but I would like to hear if there would be any objection to that. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't really have any position on that, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Would you like to make a --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it should be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on page 137, subsection (b), operation of take-over of power, then in paragraph (e) you say the allegations of the involvement of Serb forces in grave crimes in Bijeljina. And then you refer to a report of Dragan Andan to me, 65 ter 15324, but I believe it has a P or a D number. Can we have that document -- in e-court, I mean. 65 ter 15324. There is no P number? No?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, it's not admitted as yet, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You refer to it in some footnote. Mine are all different now. I believe that there is an English version. Can we have the next page in Serbian and then we're going to identify. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it's -- it's for sure mentioned in footnote 419, in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in the first bullet point down here it says "terrorising the population." Now, this policeman is describing what happened in Bijeljina and he says: "After their armed forces were destroyed by the Serb Territorial Defence ..." and so on and so forth. And he describes, inter alia, what the side effects were as the terrorising of the population, that is, after that; right? And there is no reference to a take-over of power, but actually crushing the rebellion of the Red Berets. But you are saying that that is the take-over of Bijeljina. I'm sure you remember. I can read it out, this first part, and there is no reference to take-over there. It has to do with crimes of groups that you call Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand the question because I never spoke about rebellion by Red Berets. We mentioned the obstacles erected by Green Berets or the roadblocks erected by Green Berets, which were removed, according to the reports I included, by members -- under the leadership or under the direction of the Crisis Staff, or the supervision of the Crisis Staff, and this was done by members of the local TO, Serbian national guard, and Serbian volunteer guards, and that is footnote 381. And okay, this is a report about mainly the aftermath of these events. So I don't see that as a problem that the author does not speak about a take-over. When I used the expression "take-over," I base that on a number of documents and we have discussed those documents. So the conclusion for me was that the power or the authority in Bijeljina changed and that authorities were put in place that did not respond anymore to the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that responded to authorities of the self-established Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was obviously a new creation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The report we are seeing is an identical one cited in footnote 419?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, judging by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where can we find the report number 18-3-84 here?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it should be 65 ter number 20128, that should be an identical document if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah -- excuse me, Your Honours, the reference number should be on the cover page I think. I don't think this is the first page. Because the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Thank you. Shall we upload 20128?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could it be released.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove the Serbian version completely. We can do it this way too, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the first part, it says that as is well-known after the attack of the Muslim forces, the territory of this centre of the security services, after the attack of the Muslim forces. The attack was repelled, and then it says in these paramilitary groups that you call the Serb forces tried to introduce parallel government. And there's a reference to all the things they did, and it says that their efforts were thwarted too. We will see that as well. At the end of this document you see a handwritten note of mine: "Continue with the establishment of law and order." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not see the document at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have anything? Can we have the Serbian version at least?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you bear with the court deputy until he's able to upload it and it is to be released. We have the English translation in his report so we can refer to -- refer back to 15324.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If the participants can use the report, can we have the Serbian version back. This is the cover letter signed by Mr. Andan. You know that. Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we see your handwritten note, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last page. First we're looking at the one before that -- but let's have the last page now. Let's see that too. Yes. You can see on the first page that it's sent to me. And now let's see the last page, what it is that I wrote: "Continue with the introduction of law and order." I was convinced that this had been admitted when Mr. Davidovic was here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is correct, Your Honour. I also now recognise it. It was an exhibit tendered in the -- with the Witness Davidovic, but we are just trying to locate the P number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 2 then -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this, is this the chief of the centre of the security services in Bijeljina that signed this? Whoever's reading the English version can see that. Chief of the CSB Dragan Andan, and we appointed him there because of his attitude towards the paramilitaries. After his report from Brcko and his proposed measures, we appointed him acting chief and we brought him together with Mr. Davidovic to resolve the question of the paramilitaries. Now he is reporting to me as to what was going on after the crisis in Bijeljina. And he does not say "take-over of power," because he was in power before the crisis and after the crisis. And in the first paragraph it says that an attempt was made to establish a parallel government, there were pressures against the public security station, and then in these bullet points it says terrorising the population, both Muslims and Serbs, appropriation of apartments and houses, ten persons of different ethnic backgrounds were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I take it that Mr. Theunens must have read this document, given that he's citing this document. You can put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you know that this man was in power before the crisis and after the crisis and that he was my representative up there, not the Serb forces for which you say there are allegations of involvement of Serb forces? This representative of the state is fighting against these forces that you are calling the Serb forces; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are talking about two different matters. When I talk about the Serb forces, including Arkan, I base myself on a report, footnote 380, which is actually issued by the same structure, the Bijeljina SJB, when they say that -- and again I have mentioned that a few times already, but during the night of 31st of March and 1st of April, 1992, Bosnian Serb TO, Serbian National Guard, and the Serbian Volunteer Guard, i.e., Arkan's men, under the supervision - and under the supervision I have quoted from that document - of the Bijeljina Crisis Staff start to remove barricades erected by members of the Green Berets. Now, in this document which dates from a number of months later, Mr. Andan from the Bijeljina SJB puts Mr. Karadzic on notice of crimes committed or allegedly committed by the Serbian Volunteer Guard in the aftermath of what I have described as the take-over of power in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just found it. It is P2900.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Do you accept that this man, as well as Jesuric and all the others, were in power before the crisis in Bijeljina and after the crisis in Bijeljina and that the municipal government was the same before the crisis and after the crisis and that the establishment of a parallel government did not succeed which was an attempt made by these paramilitaries --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you are coming to the issue of and meaning of taking over, I think you -- we have exhausted that issue. Why don't you move on?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that this man who expelled those forces and who is reporting to me that -- do you believe that he is the representative of Republika Srpska rather than these forces that he had expelled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, we're talking about two different matters. At one moment in time, i.e., end of March/early April, the Serbian Volunteer Guard operates in Bijeljina under the supervision of the SDS-led Crisis Staff in Bijeljina. And now this is in -- I'm just trying to find -- on the 29th of July, 1992, Mr. Andan reports about the crimes committed by the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they do that after the crisis and after getting out of -- out of the control of the Territorial Defence? Do you distinguish the moment when the volunteer unit becomes a paramilitary unit? Do you agree that the key moment is when it gets out of the chain of command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that earlier, Your Honours. In -- when they are operating under the command or the authority of the Crisis Staff, they are considered or called volunteers. And then when they conduct activities like crimes whereby it's -- from the document by Mr. Andan, it is not clear whether they have gotten out of the chain of control -- of the chain of command and control, as Mr. Karadzic puts it. But at one moment in time they started to commit crimes, and then in that context Mr. Andan qualifies them as a paramilitary group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You remember that you spoke about Mr. Blagojevic as well; right? Mr. Blagojevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, before we leave this document. I compared the two documents, i.e., 15324 and this P2900, there's differences in terms of page numbers. The former being of six pages and this five pages. Page 5 of 15324 is missing in this document, if you -- somebody take a look at it and -- in the meantime we proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the last page in English. Let us see. Probably it is the cover letter that is missing. We do have it in the Serbian version and you can see from there that he is writing to me. Yes, the last page is fine. There's this signature and there is my handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can't compare the English translation because we do not translation of 15324, but 15324 has six pages. If you could take a look later on. In the meantime, we proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you quoted Mr. Blagojevic at his press conference?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours. And this can be found in footnotes 399 until 4 -- excuse me, 401, part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say, you quote Mr. Blagojevic. You say that there was no massacre of the Muslim population. And then you interject something. You stop quoting him and you interject your own explanation, saying: "During the take-over of power ...," and then you continue quoting him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and the reason I do that because he holds his press conference on the 9th of April, and that is after the take-over of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that his qualification, this take-over of power, or did you not interject this as your own comment, you interjected this, "during the take-over"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I added this and I think it's clear from the way how it is written because there are no quotation marks and it's not in italics. So I would assume that the reader understands that this is my addition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again, I mean, footnote 400, whether you call it take-over or liberation, the result is the same. Mr. Blagojevic -- Mirko Blagojevic, for obvious reasons he talks about the combat for the liberation of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the section "The Achievement of the Strategic Objectives of the Bosnian Serbs," you quote General Mladic and analysis of combat-readiness of the Army of Republika Srpska for 1992. I have to see which paragraph that is -- or rather, which number. Which document that is. I think it's actually been admitted already. So there's an introduction, there's number 1 and number 2, and then your quotation is "both forces," it's a reference to the Serb forces before the army was established. "These forces from the very beginning of the inter-ethnic conflict in mid-March up until the 19th of May managed to protect the Serb people from bigger massacres and in part to protect the territories that are predominantly or in part populated by Serbs ...," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not find the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the objectives were that were placed before the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D351 -- no? 325, D325, that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you have quoted it and you quoted it here but my numbers are all mixed up because of what I've already explained, but I hope you know what I'm saying. That's the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, but I have quoted it several times. I'm a bit lost as to which reference you are referring to or which specific quotation you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to find it. Page 69 -- no, no, 1056, page 69 of the document in English. Page 69 in the English language. That is what it says here, in this footnote. That's not it in Serbian probably. "These forces ..." Yes, here it is. It's the fourth paragraph. "From the beginning of inter-ethnic conflict ..." Have you found it? Yes, it's the fourth paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see what General --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, remember this formulation: "... and they managed to protect the Serb people from larger massacres and the -- and managed to protect the territory." 65 ter 22551. It has to do with the first interview of General Milovanovic, the number two man of the Army of Republika Srpska, his first encounter with the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we think it is footnote 377 where this particular issue is addressed in Mr. Theunens' report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Part 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Part 2, part 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page of this interview of General Milovanovic. I cannot recognise the page itself. Can we look at the next one. Another page down, please. 9653 is the ERN number. 9653 in Serbian. The next one, please. This isn't it. The next page, please. Yes, this is it. We have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
