utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now this is what it says here: "General Milovanovic then said that the Tribunal should not try to prove the character of the war through such trials." But let's see what he says here. He asked the then-leadership for the objectives of the war, and these were the objectives: "1. To protect the Serbian people from destruction in order to avoid a repeat of events that took place between 1941 and 1945. "2. To stay within Yugoslavia, or as an alternative to this, to have our own state." Mr. Theunens, do you see the extent to which this coincides with that sentence of General Mladic and do you see that this was placed before the army as objectives, not the six strategic objectives?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I see the first point identified by General Milovanovic, to protect the Serb people from destruction, the language is quite similar to the explanation Mr. Karadzic gives to the Assembly members on the 12th of May, when he details or when he describes the first strategic goal to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you whether we ordered the army to win a -- an exit to the sea by military means or was it different --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you are asked to repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure which sentence I said last.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But were the army ordered to realise the six strategic goals or did they have only these two objectives, whereas the others were political objectives that were to be realised through talks with the European community and the other two parties?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered that question during the previous days. I have compared the six strategic goals -- no, I have compared the nine directives which are issued by the Supreme Command and/or the Main Staff of the VRS, and these directives are issued between May 1992 and September or October 1995. I have compared them with the six strategic goals and there is -- they are consistent. It is true, however, that the sixth goal, the access -- the establishing access to the sea, I haven't seen any military documents that refers to the implementation of that goal. And we discussed yesterday how that goal was indeed one of -- part of the negotiations. However, the other goals, there is, as I said, clearly a consistency between these goals and the tasks the Main Staff and Mr. Karadzic gave to the VRS throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at 65 ter 1039. This document is subject to Rule 70. I don't know why, but we needn't broadcast it publicly. This may have to be clarified. It's an interview I gave from that time, the time of my platform. Yesterday you saw my platform of 22nd April for the first time. Please do not broadcast publicly until -- until -- or as long as it's subject to Rule 70. It's no longer confidential. Or -- it says it isn't confidential and it was published in Le Figaro?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Robinson can help us in this regard. It is offered to the Defence, not to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, Mr. President, this was a document provided to us by a provider, one of the states, and they did have a blanket rule that it should all be confidential unless we get permission from them in advance. And we haven't gotten that permission, as I understand it so far with respect to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it is for you to clarify whether the provider -- to clarify as to the meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still questioning whether this is one of the documents we received directly or whether we received it from the Prosecution, given that it has an ERN number, but it may be the same situation. I'm not sure which one of us has the responsibility to clarify it with the provider, but both of us have received from the same provider newspaper articles and I'm not exactly sure which of us received this one directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, let us proceed without broadcasting this one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Serbian version also be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you read this interview, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to -- now looking at the document, there is no restriction on it any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that clarification. Yeah, it is a Figaro article -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, from my experience here, the issue may have been an issue of copyright, that the organisation that provided the article did so without necessarily having the authorisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That may have been the reason, but we heard that there's no restriction anymore so we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Serbian version Rule 70 is mentioned in line 3. That's why I was being careful. Can you see that a day after I published my platform, that is, on the 22nd of April, I'm giving an interview to this newspaper and it can also be broadcast publicly now. You see that this journalist is asking me: "According to you, all nationalities have now accepted the partition of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Why is the war continuing?" And then I reply: "On 18 March, an agreement was reached. The EEC gave its approval. The terms are clear: Three separate Bosnia and Herzegovinas will be established. They will be based on ethnic principles." And I don't want to read it out all. He mentions territory and I answered that territory is relative. And goes on to say about taking territory by force and I said that my proposal was that no territory should be seized by force. "The new map of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be based on ethnic borders that are perfectly clear. At present people are killing and being killed for nothing because at the end of the day all the territories occupied by force will have to be handed back to their inhabitants." And then he asks about Arkan and other groups. And I say that: "They are paramilitary groups. They arrived in Bosnia to respond to the infiltration by units of regular Croatian army ...," and so on. "The war is pointless. It must end." Do you know that we returned territories and throughout the war we were willing to return a good part of the territories that we held?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure whether the question refers to all the peace agreements or anything specific in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, instead of you reading out, let the witness read the document, all the document, ask -- put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, go ahead. Read the document, which clearly shows my position. And pay attention to that, my position with regard to territorial issues and that you link with the six strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we have been over this issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's a next page, second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When you're done, let us know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we can go ahead. I'm finished reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this interview touches upon some strategic objectives; Sarajevo, territorial issues, especially the fate of the territories that were taken by force or are being controlled? Do you agree that I put forward my position with regard to the six strategic objectives?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I agree that Mr. Karadzic mentions issues like Sarajevo, territorial issues, and Arkan and so on; but I do not know and I cannot establish whether he links that to the six strategic goals or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that I said just in the platform one day earlier that territories should not be taken by force because that will not be recognised; the territorial issue will be solved politically at a conference?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I'm familiar with you -- the platform you presented and where you spoke also about territorial issues, but again on the 12th of May you do present the strategic goals to the Assembly members and except - and I saw that yesterday again - for the fourth or the fifth strategic goal, there is no reference to the ongoing peace efforts whatsoever when Mr. Karadzic presents these six strategic goals to the Assembly members. And again, in the directives for further operations that are issued by the Main Staff and/or the Supreme Command to the VRS, there is no references to these -- to the platform or any other peace efforts of that time, of March/April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, all these goals were dealt with at conferences. We'll -- we'll get there yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1591, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at the ethnic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll take a brief look to see whether you are familiar with it, D225.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just like to correct the record in line 7 it should be added: "Except for the fourth or the fifth strategic goal there is no reference ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that these territories marked blue are the ones where the Serbs are the absolute majority in some places even they -- they even constitute 100 per cent of the population?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is indeed what the legend of the map states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please see Cutileiro's basic map. Please repeat the exhibit number. The green colour in the west and there's some green enclaves in the Serbian territory. Some are orange, they stand for Croats. 1D931 is the exhibit number of the Cutileiro map. Let us enlarge it a bit. Can you see that Mr. Cutileiro respected that ethnic map and he envisages enclaves or cantons in the Serbian territory and other enclaves in the Muslim territory? Can you now mark the Una river on this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you not challenge that this is the Cutileiro map?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would have to consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have -- there are some Cyrillic writing at the end. This is -- yeah, the map is written in Cyrillic or in -- written --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At the moment I am -- I can't say. We have to check what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, if you could --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- if Mr. Karadzic could explain as to the provenance of this map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the map drawn by the late Mr. Darwin who was the cartographer of the Carrington-Cutileiro team. It was drawn on plain paper and its purpose is to show the whereabouts of the Serbian, Croatian, and Muslim cantons respectively. At the time we expected there would be no war. We were about to see another map which is in line with the Muslim proposal, but for the time being what I would like Mr. Theunens to show where the following rivers are: The Una, the Sava, the Drina, the Neretva, and what the status of the Sava was to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will see what we can do with this exercise but, Mr. Theunens, if -- can you do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, without expressing any views about whether this map is authentic or not. I just draw on the screen. The Una --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yeah, you have to push the button first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just wait a minute. You know how to operate it, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think I know by now. Can I touch the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not yet. Proceed, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Una goes more or less here -- yeah, it should be close to the green line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall you put number 1, then, for Una.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Una.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it flows into the Sava up there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I remember well, the Sava is more or less for a large part on the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, but I'm not entirely sure how far it goes. It goes -- okay, north of Brcko and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With the assistance of our usher, let's change the colour for Una. We can delete the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or maybe I can use an interrupted line or something or dots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or we can change it to blue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And actually the -- I mean, if it's yellow, it goes back to this point more or less. Maybe it goes into Croatia. I don't remember exactly. But anyway, for the largest part, the border between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina in the north coincides with the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are right, but you should continue westward where the upward section of the Una stops, that's where the Sava is, and it joins the Sava in the west. The Una joins the Sava where it starts flowing straight. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, Your Honours. It's quite some time ago, but I believe Mr. Karadzic when he says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark the Drina, mark it green, let's say. Is the Drina between Serbia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Shall I proceed or ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you proceed without the assistance of our usher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which colour is going to come out of it now, but otherwise I can do it with crosses. Now it's blue, okay, it makes sense. So -- I don't remember exactly how it goes further south, but the Drina is more or less -- is more or less here. I will mark it with a 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It flows northward. Can you now mark the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Neretva goes more or less -- I would have to see where Mostar is on the map. I'm -- it's hard for me to read it, but the Neretva goes through Mostar, so I would almost say it goes here then to the coast, assuming that this dot is Mostar because my understanding is -- yeah, and then it goes further north, but I don't know exactly how it flows further north. And that would be a 4 then. But if I had a more detailed map obviously it would be easier to see where Mostar is. Because I know that, I remember that the Neretva goes through Mostar and ends up on the coast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you noted the place where Mostar is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a bit too far to the east, but okay. Can you tell us whether we are here on the Una, on the Sava, on the Drina, and on the upper flow of the Neretva which you haven't marked here, but on a more detailed map we would see that the Neretva flows also east of this number 4. And there is also Sarajevo here marked in a different colour from everything else.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the map is showing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will establish the provenance of the map since you could not confirm it. I would now just like to ask you to initial this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just put my initials --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the date, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we were not notified of this map, therefore we cannot be hundred per cent clear here and it was a bit difficult to establish. However, the Cutileiro map is part of the Exhibit P2538. And what we see in -- that's the Cutileiro Plan. And what we see in this map, that it does not correspond with what we see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- I don't remember we have seen this map --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- so that's why I suggested marking it for identification as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1592, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will prove that this is his original map. The first map -- actually, the Muslim proposal is D486. Could we please see it now. D486.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that here, both on the Una, on the Sava, on the Drina, and in the Sarajevo zone we are present and a large part of Sarajevo is coloured red and given to us. Do you agree? And we won the upper flow of the Neretva river; in other words, everywhere where we are the overwhelming majority.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't entirely agree, Your Honours, because when we look for the Una, for example, in Western Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sanski Most and Prijedor are identified here in the legend as Muslim areas and they are east of the Una. And even the -- maybe also the municipality of Bosanska Krupa goes a bit beyond -- I mean, to the east of the Una. The Sava -- okay, we see on the map there is no geographic connection between Serb areas in the west and Serb areas in the east. The Drina -- I mean, we see Muslim areas, Vlasenica, Bratunac, Srebrenica, and so on further to the south. And also for the Neretva, I don't really -- I wouldn't draw the same conclusions Mr. Karadzic does from this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I said that we're not present along the whole flow of the Una, but are we present along the Sava, the Drina, and the upper flow of the Neretva as well as Sarajevo -- in fact, all territories except on the coast? Not the entire Una is ours. The same applies for the Sava, the Drina, and the Neretva, but we are present on those rivers; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have answered the question, Your Honours, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that Sarajevo here is part of a Serbian unit and do you agree that there is no corridor and that we accepted that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my answers are based on the map I see in front of you. I'm not hundred per cent familiar anymore with the different versions of the Cutileiro Plan and how the different parties saw it or interpreted it. And -- because I didn't analyse that for the -- for this report. But here you can see that on this map Sarajevo is -- is mixed, the municipality, okay, is largely red, Serb areas. But there is also -- there is also to be a green area there. And I don't know whether the Bosnian Serbs accepted this particular map or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll establish that easily. Is it true that there is no corridor here? We have no territorial link between the red zones?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours. There is no corridor in the Sava valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D -- or rather, 1953. 1D -- I beg your pardon. 65 ter 19153.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next plan was the Vance-Owen Plan after the Cutileiro Plan; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But just for the record, the map we just saw seemed to me almost identical to the one referred to by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, which is on page 111 on that document. And I have to note that -- I have to ask you, Mr. Karadzic, this one is also prepared by the Defence team based on the information you have, using the -- using one of the maps which is in the -- in our court binder; correct, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure. This is from the documentation of the Conference on Bosnia. This is the proposal of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, who put numbers and colours on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The OTP, the OTP provided this to us. [In English] Court binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I left my court binder in my office. Do you have the court binder?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0701 is the ERN number. 0782, it's within that page range. Page 61 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Theunens, do you agree that provinces 2, 4, and 6 were marked as Serb provinces and that according to this plan we are on the Una, Sava, Drina, Neretva, and Sarajevo is extra-territorial here, it doesn't belong to anyone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I agree with the first part of Mr. Karadzic's proposition, i.e., the correspondence between the numbers and the Serb areas. Now, whether that means that the Serbs or the Bosnian Serbs are on the Una, Sava, Drina, Neretva, and Sarajevo -- excuse me, not Sarajevo, that's a matter of interpretation. I have mentioned already province 1, it goes beyond the Una to the east and the same applies to the Muslim areas number 5, I mean they are on the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we do agree, but I'm asking you whether we were on those rivers too, whether we were there as well. And is it correct that province number 3 does not belong to the Serbs; therefore, there is no corridor. Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that according to the Vance-Owen Plan there would be no corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that I accepted this map, this plan, in Athens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and this was discussed already I think yesterday or the day before, but at the end of the day the Bosnian Serbs rejected the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, mainly on the basis of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank goodness it's not the Bosnian Serbs that are being tried. I am being tried. So let us stick to what I did. Can this map be admitted, although it has been admitted in a way already. You don't really need to sign anything, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1593, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at P799, page 137. P799, Lord Owen's book. In Serbian it's page 137. We don't need to see the English because it's a drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After the Vance-Owen Plan, did the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan ensue?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did, Your Honours. I just want to emphasize that all these issues related to the various peace proposals of the international community are not discussed as such in my report. So I'm now providing answers based on my knowledge outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that all of the Una river was given to us here, also a large part of the Sava, a large part of the Drina, Sarajevo is extra-territorial, and in the valley of the Drina, in Podrinje, the Muslims had linked-up enclaves, Gorazde, Zepa, and Srebrenica. Is that right? While in Brcko we do have a corridor but we called it the T viaduct and we referred to it in different ways. It is this map on the left-hand side, on page 234.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking, Your Honours, about the map on the left, map 9; or the map on the right, map 10?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 9. That's the Owen-Stoltenberg map with regard to a union of three republics: The Serb, Croat, and Muslim. The Serb areas are white, so there is all of Una, a large part of the Sava, a large part of the Drina, and Sarajevo is under UN administration.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I can see that on the map and I would then refer to the date of the map, August 1993, where we see that in the meanwhile significant military operations have taken place in order to implement the six strategic goals. There are several directives for further operations that have been issued to the VRS, again in support of implementing the six strategic goals the VRS has made territorial gains, for example, in the east where we see the creation of the enclaves. And my conclusion would be that the plan proposed by Messrs. Owen and Stoltenberg reflects those realities on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you keep sticking to that, that our people were waging war because of the strategic objectives. Didn't they have to wage war when they were being attacked? Did they have to wage war because they were being attacked, irrespective of any strategic objectives? As a military expert, say yes or no. Is counter-offensive a legitimate military operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my report doesn't try to show whether these operations were legitimate or illegitimate. I just tried to -- tried to analyse how command and control was implemented, and analysing whether or not there was a link between the six strategic goals and the directives for further operations is, in my view, a key aspect in order to understand how command and control, especially from the highest civilian level of authority, i.e., the supreme commander, to the various commanders -- that is, in the VRS was implemented. That is all I did. It is not up to me to say whether these operations are legitimate or illegitimate or whether -- who started or who responded to whom in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the opposing side that gives directives to our army? Do you see that the Muslims are waging war to their own detriment? The longer they wage war, the worse things get for them. We had accepted plans that were far more favourable than those that were ultimately adopted; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is -- that is a subject matter that falls outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that map 10 shows how many territories we were prepared to return, territories that were at that point under our control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's -- it's maybe an issue of wording, but again for my recollection at the time and I read the book by Lord Owen, it is not so much territories the Bosnian Serbs were prepared to return but territories they would be requested to return if they would accept the maps linked to the -- to this peace plan, the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. And my recollection is that they did not accept the maps -- the map, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your recollection is wrong, Mr. Theunens. The Serbs had accepted this plan as well. I accepted it. I accepted the Cutileiro Plan. I accepted the Vance-Owen Plan. I accepted the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. And I accepted the Dayton Agreement. I only did not accept the plan of the Contact Group. Out of five plans, I accepted four. Do you know that? And most of them run against our strategic objectives, they run counter to our strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a different recollection - and again, this falls outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A different recollection being what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the Bosnian Serbs' attitude or reaction to these various peace plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But as to the -- his attitude you don't remember -- you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing I know was in relation to the Vance-Owen Plan, that indeed Mr. Karadzic initialled, I believe, part of the plan in Athens in spring 1993. My overall recollection is that the Bosnian Serbs, and Mr. Karadzic was the main negotiator for the Bosnian Serbs, their main objective -- excuse me, objection to the various peace plans were related to the maps that were presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Theunens, that I did not initial part of the plan but the entire plan in Athens, the Vance-Owen Plan, and I accepted this plan too, and the Cutileiro Plan as well. And that I accepted and created with Ambassador Holbrooke the Dayton Agreement in its entirety, and they spoiled it in Dayton later on. Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do not argue with the witness. Put your questions one by one if you like to get evidence from the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did you say "at least a part," when I accepted the entire Vance-Owen Plan in Athens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the -- my answer was based on the best of my recollection. As I said earlier, the various peace plans fall outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's asking the reason for your answer. You said I believe -- part of the plan in Athens, referring to Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do -- I mean, my recollection is that the agreement Mr. Karadzic gave was at least to the principles. The maps I'm not -- the map, I'm not hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this page be admitted, this page from Lord Owen's book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The left map, map 9, seems to me almost identical to the page 116 of Exhibit P2538, but that map -- the latter map does not -- bears the markings. We can admit this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, that's already -- it is part of an exhibit that has been already admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's part of Exhibit P799.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 06344, the map of the Contact Group plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to mention that we were not notified about the maps, so we cannot be particularly helpful here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 117 of Mr. Treanor's report is referring to Contact Group map. We'll see whether it's identical to this one or not. That's identical.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the map of the Contact Group. Do you agree that we still have access to the Una river, not the entire Una river; then also access to the Sava river. Did the Contact Group give us territorial link rather than a corridor between the east and the west? It's -- do you agree that we have also been cut off in the area of Brcko and that the Muslims have Gorazde, Zepa, and Srebrenica all together and that we are also at the upper part of the Neretva river where the Una, Sava, Drina, Neretva, and we have participation in Sarajevo that is extra-territorial yet again under the UN?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is more or less what the map represents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's already been admitted -- oh, it hasn't. Within the Treanor report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it's -- this document as such was not admitted. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1594, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 19671, the Dayton map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this map in which we were given 49 per cent of the territory, again, part of the Una, part of the Sava, a significant corridor, a wide corridor, a large part of the Drina except in Gorazde, and part of Sarajevo as well where we live to this day. Everything except for access to the sea. This plan also recognises what is defined as our political objective, not as our military objective, and this is recognised by politics, not the military.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my answer is similar to the one I gave when looking at the Contact Group peace plan map, that is, that this map again reflects the realities on the ground as they had developed through the use of military force by all sides and this is, for example, visible in Western Herzegovina, where the Federation has captured or conquered significant parts of terrain in -- during September 1995. And then, obviously, the final map is a result of political negotiations, whereby these realities in the field are taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember the first map, the ethnic map, or the first Cutileiro map, the basic map, do you remember that all these territories that we held all the time and that we finally got were inhabited by a significant Serb majority? That these are traditional Serb lands and have been so for centuries.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is Mr. Karadzic's interpretation. I think the maps speak for themselves and the colours that were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the strategic objectives were also honoured here by the international community as legitimate ones and they were all verified except for access to the sea?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that interpretation, Your Honours, because the Dayton plan also foresaw the return of people who had to leave their houses due to the war. So the separation of the Serbian people from the other two nationalities -- national communities was not respected by the Dayton plan and we can continue the discussion for the other goals as well. Sarajevo was not divided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Says who, Mr. Theunens? Do you know that there is Eastern Sarajevo that we used to call Serb Sarajevo, Eastern Sarajevo, of 100.000 people there were out of about the 200.000 people who were there and 30.000 Yugoslavs, 100.000 people stayed on and a new city was built that is called Eastern Sarajevo. And do you know that we accepted annex 7 and that people are only returning to Republika Srpska. No one's returning to the Federation. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, there's again a lot of questions about issues that fall outside the scope of my report, but if Mr. Karadzic says that the Serb Sarajevo was a newly built city, well, okay, that's fine. My understanding of the Dayton plan is that Sarajevo was handed over to the Federation, and we all remember how Serbs who were living in parts of Sarajevo that, under the implementation of the Dayton plan in the early months of 1996, were to be handed over to the Federation, that Bosnian Serbs there were called by their leadership to leave, and indeed they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: None of that is correct, Mr. Theunens. That's not part of your expert report. And the return of refugees is not part of your report and you want to harm the Defence and you are expanding the story. Why are you doing that? It is not true that we asked them to leave. We asked them to come back. It is not true that the Muslims got all of Sarajevo. They got the main part of Sarajevo, but you just don't know these things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you are not giving evidence. Just put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just a remark, it's unfair to now say that Mr. Theunens expanded. He was asked a question and he answered the question as far as he could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, would you like to comment on the last comment by the accused, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a small correction that Sarajevo was given to the Federation and the Federation consists of Muslims, or Bosniaks, and Bosnian Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that East Ilidza, East Novo Sarajevo, East Stari Grad, and Pale, and Trnovo is part of Sarajevo as well, and that that remained in Serb hands as well as Lukavica and part of Dobrinja, that Serbs did get part of their Sarajevo, they ceded Vogosca, Ilijas, the Serb part of Ilidza, the second part of Serb Ilidza and Hadzici and that is why the Muslims did not want to have Srebrenica returned to them because they liked this better? Do you know that we are there and I'm not asking you about refugees and I'm not asking you from the point of view of human rights. I'm asking you from a military point of view, from the point of view of six strategic objectives. Were they legitimate and were they recognised by all the peace plans of the international community, all of them, and ultimately verified at Dayton, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, how can the witness answer yes or no to this lengthy question? Put your question again and we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question: The basis of your report are the six strategic objectives. The Defence says that these are legitimate political objectives aimed at negotiations, and I'm asking you whether they were achieved in negotiations with the international community and the other two sides by political means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question. My conclusion is that the operations conducted by the VRS based on the operational directives that were issued by the Supreme Command and the Main Staff are coherent with the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break for 50 minutes and resume at 25 past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on page -- or, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender the previous document, the Dayton map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1595, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in the examination-in-chief on transcript page 57, lines 22 through page 59, line 3, you were asked about an order issued by Colonel - or whatever his rank may have been at the time - anyway, now he's a general, Svetozar Andric and it was admitted as Exhibit P3055 and you said that his item 6, probably an item in his order, about the relocation of Muslim population was indeed how things went. [In English] "... That his take-over was accompanied by movement of population, more specifically of non-Serbs." [Interpretation] Do we agree that this is a mistake. You say that the Serbs took over Zvornik in early May. Wasn't it in early April?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the events -- in Zvornik took, indeed, place I think in the first and second week - I mean, the take-over - of April 1992 -- the 9th and the 10th the -- is the actual date of the operation, and after that we have the aftermath with all -- I mean, with related events that are mentioned in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So did you ask yourself why that Colonel Andric waited until the 28th of May to include in his order the manner of relocation of the Muslim population. Why didn't he do so immediately? Do you have an explanation? Do you have a context that can serve to explain and shed light on that order? Or do you think that was part of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we see the document, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3055.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 6. Why as late as 28 May? If you have no explanation, that's fine, just say so.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would appreciate if Mr. Karadzic would give me the time to listen to the translation and also to read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, a number of questions have been issued. The fact that we see a reference to moving out of Muslim population on the 28th of May does not allow to draw any conclusions as to whether instructions to that effect were issued at an earlier time. Now, I have not used the terminology "ethnic cleansing" in my report. When commenting on the document during the examination I read out the paragraph and my conclusion was that this was consistent with the first strategic goal. I don't think I have commented as to the circumstances how and -- this Muslim population was moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that on 22 May, six days before this, all three parties, under the auspices of the UNHCR or the Red Cross - I don't remember which - signed an agreement that the relocation of the population from the combat zone to municipalities willing to accept them would take part in an orderly and controlled fashion. One such agreement was signed before his order and four after.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with such an agreement, so if I'm invited to comment on it, it would be helpful if I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's in evidence. I can inform you that it was signed on the 22nd in a regulated fashion with escort -- with the provision of guarantees on their own territory, civilians are to be relocated from the combat zone. And, obviously, the colonel received it within six days and included it in his order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Karadzic, if you want to further questions in relation to this issue, you should show the witness the document, as he requested. Otherwise, you just move on to other topics.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no time to display documents that are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's my impression, Mr. Theunens, that it would have been good for you to have access to these things, given the fact that you're commenting such orders; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be the case, yes. It always helps to have more information, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that in the Drina River valley about 15.000 Muslim fighters had assembled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, it would be helpful to see a document with also, like, references and dates, you know, to allow me to comment on that question or to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, fair enough. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will find some documents. I don't have time. But what I'm interested in, Mr. Theunens, if it's your conclusion that we liberated or took Podrinje because it was our objective and not because we were attacked from there, then you should know whether or not there were forces. Do you or don't you know that throughout the war, even in Srebrenica there were forces. Somebody said there was a 28th Division and in the early days of the war there were considerable forces there which incessantly attacked us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know from my professional activities prior to joining the ICTY that, indeed, there was a unit called the 28th Division of the ABiH in Srebrenica, and that, for example, end of 1992/early 1993 units of the ABiH conducted offensive operations in the wider Srebrenica -- I mean, in Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina area. But it's not part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the Muslim side declared war on Serbia and Montenegro and us, that is, they proclaimed the state of war and labelled us as enemies on 20 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may be the case. I don't have an exact recollection and, again, it falls outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, Mr. Theunens. If you are assessing the conduct of the VRS, then you should know whether war was declared on them or not; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I explained again this morning why I included the six strategic goals and also how I established that there was a consistency between the six strategic goals and the operations conducted by the VRS throughout the armed conflict. I'm not assessing the conduct of the VRS whether -- I'm not concluding whether what they did was legitimate or illegitimate; that is not up to me. I'm just looking at the simple aspect of consistency in the implementations of the principles of command and control, i.e., single authority and also establishing who held that authority, unity of command, i.e., that there was consistency in the orders of the Supreme Command and the activities of the lowest-possible-level units, as well as the obligation to implement decisions, i.e., were the orders implemented; and if they were not implemented, whether the superior who issued the orders took corrective or other action to ensure future implementation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, the question was whether you knew that war was declared.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I answered that question, Your Honours, and then there was a subsequent question by Mr. Karadzic and my longer answer now is an answer to that subsequent question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer was "that may be the case"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours. I don't recall exactly and it falls outside the scope of my report. That's in line 2 and 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You don't recall what? The date or whether the -- whether the war was declared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours. I don't remember whether war was declared. It must obviously have been the case, but I don't remember the exact wording nor a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But then you continued. It may be the case but it has nothing to do with my report. Here's my question: Would there have been operations on the part of the VRS if war hadn't been declared and would there have been VRS operations if there had been no Muslims offensives against us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the -- I think it's a very hypothetical question, but I mean if -- referring to my report I can try to give a partial answer. I understand Mr. Karadzic stated that this declaration of war was on the 20th of June. Well, the first directive for further action, and that's directive number 1, dates from the 6th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the Presidency of the VRS with my signature issued an appeal to the Muslims not to fight, that there is no point, and that their territory might eventually belong to their constituent unit and some villages accept that and stayed with us all the way through 1995 without any problem?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember seeing such a document, but if Mr. Karadzic can show it now then I can maybe try to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The document is already in evidence. Can we see 1D03913. I'm just interested whether you knew about it while you were drafting your report. 1D03913. This is an order by Sefer Halilovic -- there should be a translation. An order of the Main Staff of the armed forces in Sarajevo dated 10 July 1992. General Sefer Halilovic orders the following: "1. The Srebrenica armed forces staff shall link its free territory, the liberated territories with the free territory and the wider surroundings of the Zepa village and the wider area of the Konjevici village, Nova Kasaba, and Drinjaca, with all available forces." It seems that the translation is still not done. It says about Zvornik here -- and, actually, the following subparagraph reads: "Upon the setting up of the link with the free territory and Zepa, secure the Zepa-Zlovrh-Podravanje road with focus on holding Orlov Kamen." And then item 2: "The Zvornik armed forces staff in the area of Stara Kamenica shall attack along the axis of Kamenica-Konjevic Polje with all available forces in order to link up with the armed forces of Srebrenica and Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the following page, please. [In English] Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "3. The Srebrenica staff of the armed forces shall provide assistance to Vlasenica and Bratunac in the setting up of staffs of the armed -- of armed forces in these municipalities which would act on these free territories and which subsequently would organise armed forces in these areas." That was the 7th of July. Do you know that until the spring of the following year, this group of 15.000 soldiers constantly attacked our army from behind. You said that you know about the presence of some forces, but did you know that it was on a daily basis, those were permanent attacks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have detailed knowledge of these operations. I don't have a detailed recollection of the operations of these ABiH units nor about exact figures and the frequency and the nature of the attack because it falls outside of the scope of my report. So I didn't analyse this for the purpose of my report. I do remember that indeed they conducted -- the ABiH conducted offensive operations in the latter half of 1992 and the beginning of 1993 in Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's necessary to understand the context of the witness -- this witness's evidence, and on that ground we will admit this. Mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1596, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see 65 ter 09 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 09148.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that here in the first paragraph the document says that the forces are moving between Kamenica, Zepa, Cerska, and so on, and that they are 10.000 to 15.000 soldiers strong. The greatest concentration of these forces is in the general area of Srebrenica. The enemy is regrouping these forces in line with the purpose and goals of combat operations." And it goes on to describe where the individual things are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, instead of reading out, let the witness read the document, ask your question. That's faster and more efficient.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought that by -- that by my summarising we could save some time, but I seem to have been wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read the first part -- the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think he's going to ask a question about what is contained in para 1. So proceed to put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do we agree that it was stated that there are forces there and that there are about 10.000 to 15.000 soldiers strong, that they are regrouping, that they have combat plans, as well as that there is a war on there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, indeed, what the document states. It's the assessment of the Drina Corps -- or the assessment the Drina Corps makes of the enemy forces in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1597, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I must make a selection of documents because I cannot show them all. I will not proceed with the following documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But let me ask you about section 4, the implementation of the strategic objectives. Do you agree that if the six strategic objectives were a task given to the army, that the Chief of Staff of the VRS should know about it and the Chief of Staff is the number two man in the army? Do you agree? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean I'm not sure how we can establish whether Mr. Milovanovic knew about these goals, yes or not, at the time of the events -- I'm not sure whether we can establish that Mr. Milovanovic knew about these goals, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you are claiming that the political leadership assigned goals to the army, would it be logical for Milovanovic to know? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have answered the question. The directives -- the operational directives issued by the Main Staff, including the two signed by Mr. Karadzic, are consistent with the strategic goals, even if the strategic goals as such are not identified systematically in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The strategic objectives and the directives and the entire struggle, don't they have a common foundation and that foundation is to protect the people from massacre. That was the task that Milovanovic got: Protect the people. And that is the origin of consistency or similarity. It's not that one flows from the other, but they both flow from the same premise, that the people must be protected.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember seeing a document where Mr. Milovanovic draws that conclusion. It may well be the case, but I would like to draw your attention to footnote 361 in part 2 of the report where it -- and this is part of directive for further operations number 2, where General Mladic comments -- or he states that: "The VRS has liberated the territories we considered ours and created conditions for political and military leadership of SRBiH so that they could perform all activities and negotiations regarding the future state of BiH from the position of the stronger one in this territory." He furthermore adds: "We have broken through corridors in Eastern Bosnia and Bosanska Posavina and has made possible the century-long aspiration of the Serbian people from BiH and the Serbian Republic of Krajina to be joined with the fatherland, Serbia." This is just an example to illustrate the mind-set of the command of the Main Staff and he expresses in the directive for further operations number 2, which is dated the 22nd of July, 1992. So it goes well beyond a purely defensive effort to protect the Bosnian Serbs from massacre, as Mr. Karadzic put it in his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I take it Mr. Karadzic was referring to General Milovanovic's interview, where he said two objectives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember from this morning, Your Honours, yes. Again, that is the view Mr. Milovanovic expressed during his interview. I refer to the views the chief -- the commander of the Main Staff expresses at the time of the events, and similar views are expressed in other combat documents between May 1992 and November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I need to remind you, it's 65 ter 2251, but I believe that it was also assigned a D number. It's General Milovanovic's interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it has been admitted, 22551, and at the time you didn't tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I seek to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to tendering this. This is a summary of a meeting that the Prosecution had with this General Milovanovic and I don't really see how that can be admitted according to the rules that this Trial Chamber has established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember what Mr. Theunens commented on, but -- I would like to see the page. Give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D22551 and then 06089653, I believe it's page 7. The ERN number ends in 653. These are minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is what Mr. Theunens answered: "When I see the first point identified by General Milovanovic to protect the Serb people from the destruction, the language is quite similar to the explanation Mr. Karadzic gives to the Assembly members on the 12th of May when he detailed or described the first strategic goal to them." So in that sense I think we had a basis to admit that page for the reference purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For reference purpose, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll admit that page. Give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1598, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, are you saying that this coincidence between the efforts to secure the people and strategic goals is in place or do you think that the strategic goals were actually given to the army as a task?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both apply, actually. When Mr. Karadzic explained the first strategic goal at the Assembly session, he refers to the need or indirectly he refers to the need to protect the Serbs and that in his view that can only be achieved by separating the Serbs from what he calls their enemies or our enemies. And in addition -- I mean, the second part of the question, the strategic goals - as I mentioned several times - it is my conclusion that these strategic goals serve as the basis for the operational directives and subsequent orders and commands throughout the VRS chain of command for the units to conduct military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that a mere coincidence or is it something that the leadership tasked the military with? It's a simple question. Did you find proof to show that the army received that, not as a basis for negotiations, but that it was something it was tasked with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not seen a document that -- I mean, a document from the Supreme Command stating that the military has to or the Main Staff has to implement the six strategic goals. It would be helpful -- I mean, just for the context to maybe see the document Mr. Krajisnik issues on the 12th of May with a decision on the six strategic goals because maybe that wording will allow me to provide a more precise answer. And that document is included in footnote 163.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document has P number 00955.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the issue of the Official Gazette and the date be shown when it was published. Could we please see the Official Gazette. Or let's go about it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that it was only published in the autumn of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That has been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you do not have any proof of that being given to the military as a task and it was made public only in 1993. Can we now, once you've read it, 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having seen this document, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I can just read the date. Apparently, according to the Gazette, it was also published in 1993, but I don't think that that allows to conclude that it was only published in 1993, at least not on the basis of the documents I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have proof of it having been made public sometime before that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the actual document, Your Honours? No, I don't have proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3934.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We saw what General Milovanovic said in his interview with the OTP. Let us see what he said when he testified in the Tolimir case on the 18th of May, 2011. Can we have the next page. Please take a look at this from line 5 onwards. Let us see what General Milovanovic, who was number two man of the army throughout the war, says.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the page, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page as well and then I'm going to put a question, lines 6 through 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it seem logical to you now, Mr. Theunens, that the six strategic objectives were envisioned for negotiations? Had they been envisioned for the military, they would have been put in the form of an order to the military.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have -- I have answered that question several times. It is my conclusion -- and again, we also see that from the operations the VRS conducts as well as, actually, the evolution in the various peace proposals and the maps that are presented by the international mediators during the conflict, that is, that the VRS implements these goals, on the basis of directives for further operations, and that results in changes on the terrain, together, of course, also with changes imposed by the other parties, especially leading to the map that was presented in Dayton and that is then the basis for negotiations. As I mentioned yesterday when Mr. Karadzic presents the six strategic goals to the Assembly members, he doesn't describe it as a basis for political negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that on the 9th of June it was concluded that the maps be sent to the European Community along with them, with the aim of negotiating? We have shown that document. You don't have to answer. We've all seen this. Let me ask you something else. Is it correct that, by way of analogy, you conclude that if things developed in a certain way on the ground that had to be due to the six strategic objectives?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the question is rather unclear. What is meant by "if things developed in a certain way on the ground"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have no proof that the directives and order and conduct of the army were based on an explicit order based on the six strategic objectives; however, you do conclude that on the basis of what the army was doing this must have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we're done with this. He answered the question several times.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can these two pages be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it is for reference purposes only, I have no objection. Otherwise, it is actually read into the record. I see no real purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You may call General Milovanovic, Mr. Karadzic. We'll not admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Prosecution is going to be calling him unless they give up because he's on the list, Milovanovic I mean. If General Milovanovic does not come, I ask that this and that be admitted. 1D3935, can we have that now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Krajisnik's testimony. He was the speaker of the Assembly. It's probably the Popovic case. It's from line 13 onwards. I don't have to read it out. Could you please have a look at that up to page, or rather, line 20.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read that section.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now from 5 until 13.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this differ now from what you thought about this until now?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krajisnik is testifying the same as you have been -- as Mr. Karadzic has been saying in court. I mean, it doesn't change my view. If you look at the principles of command and control on one hand -- I mean, you look at the doctrine on one hand and then how it was implemented by the Supreme Command and the Main Staff on the other hand, it is hard to imagine that the objectives the VRS pursued which actually didn't change during the war, that they were just the result of self-imagination or coincidence or anything else the VRS, the Main Staff, implemented the instructions of the Supreme Command. There are two directives for further operations that are signed by Mr. Karadzic, and, again, the objectives that are included in these directives for further operations are fully consistent with the six strategic goals. It may also have been that these were used during negotiations, but again that would show the consistency between the political and military goals the Bosnian Serbs pursued during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the Serb territorial claims pertain to Serb territories, that -- territories that they have been inhabiting for centuries and where they were a majority and that they were even ready not to have all of them included, from 44 to 52 -- we stopped at 49 actually. So the political leadership, did it place an order before the military asking them to take something that had not been Serbian?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot answer that question because I don't know -- I mean, I'm not a demographer and I don't know how or what territory was inhabited exactly by Serbs and on when and so on. So it's -- it falls outside the scope of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Different from the past practice and quite correctly, Mr. Karadzic put the question without reading out the transcript, instead asking the witness to read out. So in order to understand the context of this witness's evidence, probably we -- for the reference purpose we need to admit those transcript pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll admit the previous Milovanovic's transcript pages, i.e., T-14276 and the next page 14277, and these two pages as well. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be Exhibits D1599 and D1600, respectively.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for reference purposes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I heard from my advisors that the indictment cannot be evidence, so I wonder whether perhaps this entire report cannot be admitted at all because it looks like an indictment more as an expertise. Maybe it can only be taken as a reference. There's a mistake in the transcript. I asked my advisors whether the indictment can be evidence and I was told that it cannot. So this report cannot be evidence either. Maybe it should just be marked for reference because it looks like an indictment more than an expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unnecessary and improper comment, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at how things stand with the operative directives of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. That is item 1 and then (A) is the introduction. Can I ask for D00325 now. Let us see what is being planned by our foe, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and what lies in store for the Serbian side. No, no, D00325, it says the aim of the operations in the Muslim offensive: To concentrate part of the forces and to deblockade Sarajevo with the simultaneous engagement of part of the forces, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did you know what the military objective of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that we have -- we should have the correct document. Do you have the page number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D232. I seem to have asked for the wrong number. Page 7 in this analysis. Please, let us look at page 7 of this analysis. Actually, let's leave the previous one, 325, D325.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You cite that page, 325. I believe that you referred it to in a footnote.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document is mentioned in -- it's the first, excuse me, directive for further action. It's footnote 359 in part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm interested in seeing part of this analysis, D325, page 7 in English. Page 7, is that page 7? In English, I don't think this is page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is both in e-court and hard copies page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read it out in English. "The objective of the operations ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreter doesn't follow. Is it third paragraph on this page?
