utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the objective of our operations, that's paragraph 3, whereas this has to do with the Muslim objectives.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot find it in either language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the aim of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was to deblockade Sarajevo and to liberate all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is outside the scope of my report, but I remember from my work prior to joining ICTY that -- I think at the latest end of 1993 the then-Chief of the General Staff of the ABiH, General Delic, announced what he called "the Liberation War." That was indeed intended to what he described as liberating the whole of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm not fully familiar anymore with the goals of the ABiH at an earlier stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we find something in your report now -- sorry, just a moment. Operative directives of the Main Staff, that's the chapter I'm looking for. I'll find it in a moment. Just a second. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It starts at footnote 357, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Part 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's page 118, if this is correct. 1034 is the number I have but all of this has been mixed up. 65 ter is 01717. On page 7 of that document you actually identify the actions and plans of the Muslim army; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would be helpful to see the document because I'm not sure whether I understand what Mr. Karadzic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the operative directives, this page 118, if that is correct. Can we have that in e-court, 118, that's a page from your document, your report, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The operational directives start in the merged document in the English at page 130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not 127?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is in the old version, Your Honours, of part 2, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever. Let's just have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are going to put question in relation to his expert report, we all have it so you can proceed to ask the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you noticed, Mr. Theunens, that the objectives of our enemies were to cut the corridor, to take territories, and also that they were mercilessly dealing with the Serb people and prisoners, that they were trying to legalise their illegal procurement of weapons; is that right? That is what is contained in the document that you referred to in a footnote.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these directives for further operations do include a paragraph on enemy forces, and it may well be that the information that is now provided by Mr. Karadzic is included there. But it doesn't mean that I have verified whether this information is accurate or not because that was not part of my responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, what is in e-court seems to be an old version. This is page 130.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was looking at a different version. It's -- this is -- it would be 12 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is identical to what I have and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- Mr. Theunens said it was an old version. Yes, shall we go back to then 127 Mr. Karadzic is referring to. Probably next page. Yes, what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that our army identified the objectives and plans of our military foes, as is stated here, however, I don't know how much is contained in your text and how much is contained in the footnote that I called up and included in my question. The ERN number of the footnote that you referred to is 00607339 up until 7480. That is what you referred to. You referred to that document in this regard.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and that ERN corresponds with the -- with footnote 355, that is, the analysis of the combat-readiness, whereby I use that as an introduction to the section on -- where I discuss the directives for further operations in detail. Because -- and we have seen that passing when you were going through e-court. The analysis of the combat-readiness highlights the functioning or the functioning of the system of command and control including the single authority. And also the consistency between the political goals and the military objectives that follow from these political goals, and that's why I included a reference to this analysis of the combat-readiness in the introduction to the section on the operational directives or directives for further operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have to show the page 365 in e-court and next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, in the middle of the page footnote 355.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that (a), (b), (c), and (d) are your interpretation. You are stating items from direction number 1 and in parenthesis there is your explanation to which directive this refers. "Secure parts of Sarajevo with a Serbian population majority"; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, I added the references to the strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did General Mladic add that he was acting pursuant to the order in connection with the fifth strategic goal or is it only logical for him to protect his people? Does he make any reference to the fifth strategic goal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him making a specific reference to the fifth strategic goal. I added this reference because it was my conclusion that this specific task, i.e., securing the parts of Sarajevo that have a majority Serb population, serves the implementation of strategic goal number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It serves or coincides with. That is, the army received this as a task and that's why it wants to protect the Serbs in Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's at least two questions here. Again, based on my understanding of how command and control was implemented in the SRBiH and then in the RS and with the VRS, I don't think -- it's not my conclusion that things happened by coincidence, and again referring to the analysis on the combat-readiness. The well-functioning and the effective functioning of the system of command and control is highlighted there. And the second part of the question, the protection of the Serbs in Sarajevo, I have not found that in that specific document, I believe. It may well be that that was one of the goals that was pursued, but it was not explicitly put in that directive as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come it made its way to a document? Where did it come from? Can we see directive number 1? It says here directive for subsequent action number 1 and four operative goals are mentioned, (a), (b), (c), and (d). (A), (b), (c), and (d) are from the Mladic document and what we see in brackets is your understanding of the documents and your understanding of the link with these strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is not in brackets, is it part of directive 1?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, even if I may have summarised the text, we would have to compare the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Directive 1 is D232. Can we see it now, lest we should forget where we are. The rest of it, (b), (c), and (d), contain any reference of Mladic's to six strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the following page. You have seen under item 2 that the army got the task to launch offensive action with limited goals and thus improve its position. But there's no mention of six strategic goals anywhere; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, and I've mentioned that earlier. And again, the goals as I have mentioned them in footnote 359 can be found in the section "The Goal of the Action." But there is no explicit reference to the six strategic goals, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the segment that reads: "I decided ..." It's on page 4 or page 5. We can leaf through until we find the decision. It must be the following in Serbian. Can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Or possibly it's on page 1 under item 4. Can we go back to the first page. Yes, here it is. "I decided defend the lines already attained by means of persistent and active defence; prevent infiltration of sabotage groups and infiltration of enemy groups in the main directions; by using a part of our forces, implement active offensive actions in order to mop-up the territory or mop-up remaining groups and individuals belonging to the enemy in the territory; provide secure communication ..." and so on. Is -- does this reflect military logic, Mr. Theunens, justified and legitimate military logic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is yeah, the decision of the command of -- it's not up to me to decide whether it is justified, or to establish whether it is justified or not. That is the overall task he sets for the VRS, and that is further -- is then further specified in the tasks of the subordinate units and the specific territorial goals he sets for these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that until the setting up of the army we more or less attained all our strategic goals, apart from the corridor which wasn't really a goal before the war. Do you know that the army basically inherited all territories? The lines in Sarajevo were drawn on the 5th of April, and then we only gradually lost territory without gaining any and the entire Serb territory was protected before we had an army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is a judgement or a conclusion one can draw with insight, I mean, after the events. The question that would be -- could be raised would be then: What were the expectations -- what were the goals at the time? And actually there we find the answers in the six strategic goals and the directives for further operations. The directives for further operations are not just limited to consolidating control over the terrain that is already under Serb control, but over the years they also include instructions to obtain control over additional territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're trying to say that at the end of the war we had more territory than at the beginning. I'm saying that at the beginning of the war, before the army was established, controlled nearly all our territories. We had more and later on we lost territory. And you said that these directives were used to conquer more territory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's a question of logic. It is correct that the VRS -- but I doubt whether it was in May 1992. My understanding is that by the end of 1992 the VRS controls approximately 70 per cent of the territory of BiH. And it is correct that with the Dayton Agreement they only -- only between brackets obtained 49 per cent. But that is a conclusion or a judgement that we can make after the operations and it doesn't exclude -- I mean, the fact that they had 49 at the end has, in my view, nothing to do with the fact that throughout the conflict instructions are given to capture additional terrain. The other parties were also obviously involved in the conflict, they conducted offensive operations, sometimes defensive, and all that had an effect on the degree to which the directives for further operations were implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Theunens, I kindly ask you to leave aside logic and analogies and go back to the facts. My question was clear: Didn't we have most at the beginning and later on only lost? And where did you find an order to take territory belonging to others? Is there such an order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he not answer the question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't answer that there was an order. He said that it was logical, and I have a problem with logic and analogies and understanding here. I don't have a problem with facts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think that's an accurate representation of -- of my answer. What I was trying to say is that at -- during the conflict one could not predict the outcome of the conflict. And so it is a bit of a strange judgement to try to justify the outcome or to use the outcome of the conflict as a justification for what the intentions were at the beginning of the conflict because it is not just one party that determines or influences the outcome of the conflict. The VRS controlled more than 70 per cent of the territory of BiH by end of 1992. As a result of the Dayton Agreement the Bosnian Serbs obtained 49 per cent. Now, I have not seen in the directives for further operations any instructions as to limit or reduce the extent of the ground or terrain controlled by the VRS. Mr. Karadzic asked whether I have seen any instruction on how to capture additional terrain. Just referring, and we have mentioned that in directive number 7 which is signed by Mr. Karadzic and that is footnote 371, we're talking about the physical separation of Srebrenica and Zepa. And it talks about definitely liberating the Drina Valley. Now, it's not my task to determine whether the Drina Valley belonged to party A, B, or C, or whatever. But in the peace plans or the various maps we saw this morning, we saw a number of maps that indicated that the Drina Valley in fact -- or that there were districts, like in the Cutileiro Plan, that would be attributed or stay under the control of the Muslims. And that is just one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, did you find my statements that we don't want to defeat the Muslims and that we don't want to wage war for territory, but favour a political solution? And can we agree that the goal of the Serb side was to preserve Serbian territory and that the goal of the Muslim side was to conquer all of Bosnia? As a soldier, you should know that. What was the objective of the Serb side, to take all of Bosnia or to preserve what they have? And what was the objective of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's again a lot of questions. I can only refer to my report, and there, it is my conclusion that the six strategic goals were the basis for the operation -- excuse me, the operations conducted by the VRS as a result of the directives for further operations that were issued by the Main Staff and the Supreme Command to the VRS. I have not analysed the goals or the war goals of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that apart from directive 2 you mention Mladic's words who said, We have liberated the territories we consider ours and created conditions for the political and military leadership of the SRBH to engage in all talks on the future structure of BH from the position of the stronger party? So the final word will be said in negotiations; correct? Is it correct that Mladic here does not suggest "uti possidetis juris" but instead he says that it will be solved in negotiation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic says what he says. He does mention negotiations, but he doesn't say that the conflict will be solved through negotiations. He just states that the actions and the activities of the VRS allow the political leadership, and actually the military leadership too, to perform all activities and negotiations concerning the future of BiH from the stronger position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That means the holding of territory has to -- tactical rather than strategic importance. It means that the Serbs will be returned it when peace is achieved. Lord Owen said that it hasn't yet happened in history that an army that is undefeated returns 30 per cent of the territory. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I don't remember anymore this statement or this alleged statement by Lord Owen, but he may well have said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the BBC's film about Yugoslavia, these are the words of Lord Owen. But Mladic, in sound mind, states that whatever's done is done for the purpose of negotiations and not with the attitude: What we take will remain ours.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we would have to look at when Mladic makes that statement, in which circumstances, and then further -- also look at the context, and then maybe I'm in a position to comment. I mean, in the paragraph we quoted now, 361, Mladic mentions negotiations, but he says actually "could perform all activities and negotiations." So it's not restricted just to negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, sir. This is the 22nd of July, 1992, directive number 2. This is on the following page, and you comment there that it was issued and refers to the cease-fire agreement reached in London and so on, and under (b) you quote Mladic as saying that he said that the army has created a good negotiating position. And you know what "uti possidetis juris" means, the rightful ownership of that which one possesses. Is that what Mladic says here or does he say that we have created a favourable negotiating position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we dealt with it. You can move on to next topic. We dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The third directive, Mr. Theunens, was published on 3 August 1992 and you state on the following page that its goals are: Prevent the lifting of the blockade of Sarajevo and the arrival from -- of Ustasha forces from Croatia. And in brackets you add which is in line with strategic goals 2 and 5; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I have added the references to the strategic goals. The other text, I mean in the small print, is taken from the directive. This is footnote 362, part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see from this directive that our enemy is planning to lift the siege of Sarajevo, break through from Central Bosnia toward Posavina, that is, the corridor, breaking through toward Eastern Bosnia and breaking through from the Cazin Krajina and towards Central Bosnia and directive 3 doesn't say that Sarajevo and Central Bosnia are to be taken, but rather what we already have should be preserved; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the directive doesn't say that Sarajevo should be taken, which is again consistent with the strategic goal number 5 which is -- consists of maintaining the division of Sarajevo. And I just would like to add that is -- also mention is made of offensive operations. So it's not just of keeping what one -- or preserve what one has, but also to conduct offensive operations, and offensive operations are normally intended to obtain additional terrain or achieve control of additional terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you see why? To create a favourable negotiating position in the talks with the Muslim-Croat coalition. I'm reading from the Serbian translation, but I'm sure you can find the relevant section. It's right on the following page. It says here: Tactical advance toward Majevica and other mountains, but it also states the reasons to take dominant features in order to create a favourable negotiating position.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, but it refers to other -- to operations in other territories, not Sarajevo, Central Bosnia-Herzegovina, or the towns that are identified -- I mean, geographic objectives that are identified under the previous paragraph "offensive operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But the purpose of creating a more favourable negotiating position remains. Isn't that what it says literally?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that section it does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how the crisis in the Kotor Varos municipality developed when the village of Vecici demanded that the civilians be released, whereas they wanted to stay behind and fight? Do you know about that? It's the very beginning of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with that because that falls outside the scope of my report. I didn't deal with matters that occurred in the territory of -- corresponding with the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that the combat operations in the war in Eastern Bosnia, the issue was raised and it was General Morillon, applications were submitted to him to make possible the departure of Muslim civilians from Podrinje to Tuzla and our condition was the release of Serbia civilians from Tuzla so they may leave the territory controlled by the 2nd Corps of the BH army. Did you know about that? You had to come across these documents.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember coming across such documents during the preparation of this report. But again, if Mr. Karadzic wants to show me documents, I can try my best to analyse them and answer his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I would like to know is what you knew when you were writing the report. I don't want you to write another report, that will not happen. I want to find out what you knew and what you didn't. We'll now deal with directive number 4. Does it refer to Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just reading the text. It's footnote 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just two pages -- yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Footnotes 363 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are having -- we have it on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ah, okay. Excuse me, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It doesn't mention Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page where the aims of the operations are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First: Crush and drive out the regular units of the Armed Forces of Croatia from the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. Then preserve the free territories on all fronts, set up a border service, stabilise the existing corridors and open new ones to ensure unimpeded communication in the RS. And you add that this corresponds to strategic goal 2, and I say this coincides to the logic of survival, and not strategic goal 2; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the logic of survival is the interpretation of Mr. Karadzic. When I see stabilising existing corridors and opening new ones, the logical conclusion would be -- and when comparing that with the strategic goals is to look at the strategic goals and determine whether there is a strategic goal that refers to corridors and then strategic goal number 2, i.e., establishing a corridor between Semberija and Krajina, is the logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to rise for today, Mr. Karadzic. I take it that you evidently need more time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? Oh, absolutely. Can we work for longer than one hour tomorrow, with our appreciation to the staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have another official commitment. You have spent about ten hours and 40 minutes. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, 20 minutes would be enough for your re-examination -- or Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You will have 40 minutes. Try to conclude in 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we rise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- you asked a question about the Exhibit P2900 in relation to the missing page, and we have found out that you are absolutely correct. There is a page missing, both in the English and in the B/C/S. However, 65 ter 15324, that's the item that Mr. Karadzic put forward, is complete, both in the English and in the B/C/S. So I think it's probably the best to replace the one with the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. But do we have the English translation for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We didn't have it at the time when I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. But now it is uploaded -- yeah, it is uploaded and it can be replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Directive 3, as far as I understand matters, hasn't been admitted. Can it be admitted? The witness and his report deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was the 65 ter number? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's footnote 362, but I don't --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6314, that's what it should be, 6314, that should be the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: As far as I can identify it from the footnote, it should -- it should be 65 ter 01600.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. I can't comment -- but I'll leave it in the hands of the court deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With confirmation from the parties. We'll admit directive number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 01600 is Exhibit D235.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, it's already in the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 11.00, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 22nd day of July, 2011, at 11.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.03 p.m.,
